title: Vice President, Finance
description:
About Junior Achievement of Tampa Bay

Junior Achievement of Tampa Bay believes every student deserves an opportunity-filled future - one shaped by choices, not chance. Through experiential learning in financial literacy, career readiness, and entrepreneurship, JA helps young people become confident, capable, competent, and connected to economic opportunity.

Working alongside schools, businesses, volunteers, and community partners, JA equips students with the transferable skills, real-world experiences, and relationships they need to pursue continuing education and training, navigate an evolving workforce, and achieve economic mobility. By connecting classroom learning to high-growth, high-demand career pathways, JA prepares young people to build financially secure futures and confidently navigate what comes next. Learn more at our website:

Position Summary

The Vice President of Finance provides strategic financial leadership and oversight to ensure the organization's financial sustainability, accountability, and long-term growth. This position is responsible for financial planning, budgeting, accounting, cash management, financial reporting, internal controls, audit coordination, grant compliance, and risk management.

As a key member of the executive leadership team, the Vice President of Finance partners with the President, Board of Directors, Finance Committee, and department leaders to support informed decision-making, responsible stewardship of resources, and alignment of financial strategies with the organization's mission and strategic priorities.

The ideal candidate is a strategic and hands-on financial leader with strong nonprofit accounting experience, exceptional analytical skills, and the ability to translate complex financial information into clear, actionable recommendations.

​​​Essential Functions

Financial Strategy and Leadership

  • Develop and implement financial strategies that support the organization's mission, strategic plan, and long-term sustainability.
  • Serve as a financial advisor to the President and executive leadership team.
  • Evaluate financial performance, identify trends and risks, and recommend strategies to strengthen financial health.
  • Develop financial forecasts, cash flow projections, and long-range financial plans.
  • Evaluate the financial implications of new programs, facilities, partnerships, grants, and organizational initiatives.
  • Establish and maintain financial policies, procedures, and best practices consistent with nonprofit accounting standards.

Budgeting and Financial Planning

  • Lead the annual operating and capital budgeting process in collaboration with the President and department leaders.
  • Prepare and present the annual organizational budget for executive and Board approval.
  • Monitor actual financial performance against budget and provide timely variance analyses and corrective recommendations.
  • Develop and maintain multi-year financial projections and scenario analyses.
  • Establish appropriate budget controls and monitor departmental spending.
  • Support program and facilities expansion through financial modeling, cost analysis, and resource allocation planning.

Accounting and Financial Reporting

  • · Oversee the organization's accounting operations, including general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll accounting, cash management, and account reconciliations.
  • Ensure accurate and timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
  • Oversee the preparation of the statement of financial position, statement of activities, statement of cash flows, and supporting schedules.
  • Maintain accurate accounting for restricted and unrestricted contributions, grants, pledges, and other revenue sources.
  • Oversee revenue recognition, expense allocations, prepaid expenses, fixed assets, depreciation, accrued liabilities, and other accounting functions.
  • Maintain an effective monthly and year-end financial close process.
  • Ensure financial records are complete, accurate, and maintained in accordance with applicable requirements.

Board and Finance Committee Support

  • Prepare and present financial reports, forecasts, budget updates, and financial analyses for the Board of Directors and Finance Committee.
  • Explain financial results, budget variances, cash flow trends, and financial risks in clear, understandable terms.
  • Provide recommendations regarding reserves, investments, capital expenditures, and long-term financial sustainability.
  • Support the development and monitoring of financial policies and organizational performance measures.
  • Ensure Board members have the financial information necessary to fulfill their fiduciary responsibilities.

Grant Accounting and Compliance

  • Oversee financial management and reporting for government grants, foundation grants, corporate sponsorships, and other restricted funding.
  • Ensure grant expenditures comply with award terms, approved budgets, and applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
  • Coordinate with program leaders and grant administrators to monitor budgets, expenditures, matching requirements, and reporting deadlines.
  • Maintain appropriate documentation to support grant expenditures and financial reports.
  • Oversee the preparation of financial schedules for grant monitoring, audits, and funder reviews.
  • Establish procedures to ensure restricted funds are properly tracked, allocated, and used for their intended purposes.

Audit, Compliance, and Internal Controls

  • Coordinate the annual independent financial statement audit and serve as the primary financial liaison with external auditors.
  • Oversee the preparation of audit schedules, reconciliations, supporting documentation, and financial disclosures.
  • Maintain effective internal controls to safeguard organizational assets and prevent fraud, errors, and misuse of funds.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable nonprofit financial reporting requirements, tax filings, and regulatory obligations.
  • Oversee preparation and filing of Form 990 and related financial information in coordination with external tax professionals.
  • Monitor compliance with financial policies, contractual obligations, and relevant accounting standards.
  • Implement corrective actions in response to audit findings and recommendations.
  • Support enterprise risk management, insurance reviews, and financial risk mitigation.

Cash Management and Resource Stewardship

  • Monitor cash balances, liquidity, receivables, payables, and operating reserves.
  • Develop cash flow forecasts to ensure sufficient funds are available to meet operational commitments.
  • Oversee banking relationships, account reconciliations, authorized signatories, and cash management procedures.
  • Monitor investment activity and ensure funds are managed in accordance with Board-approved policies.
  • Evaluate major purchases, equipment investments, facility improvements, and other capital expenditures.
  • Recommend strategies to maximize the responsible use of financial resources.

Payroll, Benefits, and Financial Administration

  • Oversee the financial aspects of payroll, employee benefits, retirement plan contributions, and related reconciliations.
  • Ensure payroll liabilities, employer taxes, benefit deductions, and retirement contributions are accurately recorded and remitted.
  • Coordinate with payroll providers, professional employer organizations, benefits administrators, and retirement plan vendors.
  • Maintain appropriate segregation of duties and authorization controls over payroll and employee-related transactions.
  • Ensure financial procedures related to employee compensation and benefits are properly documented and monitored.

Systems, Processes, and Operational Efficiency

  • Oversee the financial accounting system and related reporting tools to ensure data integrity and effective financial analysis.
  • · Identify opportunities to improve accounting processes, automate routine tasks, and strengthen reporting capabilities
  • Establish standardized financial procedures, documentation requirements, and approval workflows.
  • Collaborate with technology vendors and internal stakeholders to maintain effective financial systems and reporting.
  • Develop dashboards and performance indicators that support timely financial decision-making.

Leadership and Collaboration

  • Lead, supervise, and develop finance and accounting personnel.
  • Establish clear performance expectations, accountability measures, and professional development goals.
  • Foster a culture of accuracy, transparency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Work closely with program, development, operations, and administrative teams to align financial management with organizational priorities.
  • Promote responsible stewardship of donor contributions and other organizational resources.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration.
  • CPA, MBA, or other relevant advanced professional credential preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum of 7–10 years of progressively responsible accounting and financial management experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading budgeting, financial reporting, accounting operations, and audit preparation.
  • Nonprofit accounting experience strongly preferred, including knowledge of fund accounting and restricted contributions.
  • Experience managing grants, government funding, or other restricted awards preferred.
  • Experience presenting financial information to executive leadership, Boards, or Finance Committees.
  • Experience supervising and developing accounting or finance staff.
  • Experience with accounting systems, financial reporting tools, and process improvement initiatives. Skilled in Sage Intact and Martus software a plus

Desired Qualifications

  • Strong knowledge of GAAP and nonprofit financial reporting requirements.
  • Understanding of Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) guidance applicable to nonprofit organizations, including contribution accounting and net asset classifications.
  • Knowledge of nonprofit budgeting, cash management, internal controls, and financial risk management.
  • Ability to analyze complex financial information and communicate findings to nonfinancial audiences.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • High level of integrity, discretion, accountability, and professional judgment.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Proficiency with accounting software, Microsoft Excel, and financial reporting systems.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships with staff, auditors, donors, Board members, and external partners

Compensation & Benefits

The salary range for this position is $125,000 to $135,000 annually, with the exact salary depending on relevant experience, demonstrated executive-level impact, and alignment with the scope and responsibilities of the role. JA Tampa Bay offers medical, dental, and group life insurance. The organization also offers a 401(k) plan.

Our Leadership Philosophy

At Junior Achievement of Tampa Bay, leadership extends beyond managing functions - it is about stewarding people, partnerships, and resources in service of our mission. Leaders are expected to think strategically, collaborate across teams, cultivate authentic relationships, and create the conditions that enable others to succeed. Through integrity, innovation, accountability, and a commitment to continuous improvement, every leader contributes to building a culture where philanthropy, learning, and organizational excellence work together to create lasting impact for the young people and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

At JA of Tampa Bay, we believe that our success is directly tied to our ability to foster an environment where all individuals have access to opportunities and can thrive. We are deeply committed to creating a workplace where inclusion and belonging are not just principles but lived experiences. This commitment drives us to attract, develop, retain, and promote a workforce that mirrors the communities we serve, bringing together a wide range of perspectives, experiences, and talents.

We embrace the unique contributions that every JA Tampa Bay employee brings to our mission and encourage individuals from all backgrounds to join our team. By welcoming various voices, we continue to expand our understanding of the world, and we actively seek to elevate the representation of different individual experiences and the perspectives they shape.

We are dedicated to fostering an environment where everyone feels respected, valued, and heard - where people can be their authentic selves and know that they belong. This is how we build a workplace where every individual can succeed, and where we work together to create lasting impact for the young people and communities we serve.

Additional Information

title: Engineer, Manager - MRB/Sustainment
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Air Dominance and Strike Aerostructures Engineering Team is responsible for designing and analyzing advanced structural parts for Group 5 air vehicles and missile platforms. Air Dominance and Strike Structures Engineers own the full development lifecycle, from conceptual to detailed design and analysis of primary and secondary structures, ensuring high-performance, resilient, and scalable mechanical systems that meet the demands of complex, contested environments.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Lead and grow a team of MRB analysis and sustainment design engineers responsible for dispositioning non-conformances and releasing repair solutions for metallic and composite structures on Group 5 air vehicles
  • Own the end-to-end health of the MRB system — from non-conformance intake and structural substantiation through repair drawing release and production closure — ensuring the team meets schedule, quality, and airworthiness requirements
  • Hire, mentor, and develop analysis and design engineers, including establishing a path to MRB signature/delegated authority for team members
  • Set technical standards and review complex or high-risk dispositions and repair designs, acting as an escalation point for the most difficult non-conformances
  • Partner with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing Engineering, Design, Materials & Processes (M&P), and Program Management to prioritize work, resolve cross-functional blockers, and protect production schedule
  • Drive root cause and corrective action (RCCA) programs to reduce recurring non-conformances, rework, and scrap across the production line
  • Build and continuously improve MRB processes, tools, and standard work to scale the team as production rates increase
  • Report on team throughput, non-conformance trends, and open risk to engineering and program leadership
  • Balance team workload across analysis and design disciplines, ensuring tight hand-offs between disposition and repair drawing release

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent experience
  • 8+ years of experience in aerospace structural analysis, design, or liaison engineering, with direct MRB or non-conformance disposition experience
  • 2+ years of experience leading or managing engineers, either as a people manager or in a senior technical leadership capacity

Hoe ziet het team eruit?

Je werkt binnen een Customer Team met verschillende functionele en technische specialisten. Daarnaast werk je nauw samen met:

  • Service Delivery Manager (SDM): richt zich op de kwaliteit van de dienstverlening, de serviceafspraken en de bijbehorende processen.

  • Technical Lead Consultant (TLC): vervult een vergelijkbare rol als de BLC, maar dan vanuit technisch perspectief. De TLC kijkt naar de technische architectuur, de samenhang tussen systemen, integraties en toekomstige technische ontwikkelingen en optimalisaties.

Als First Contact voer jij de dagelijkse functionele regie. De BLC en TLC kijken meer naar de tactische en strategische ontwikkeling van de klant.

Wie zoeken we?

We zoeken een Functional Consultant die zelfstandig analyses kan uitvoeren en problemen kan oplossen. Daarnaast:

  • Heb je ervaring met Dynamics 365 F&O met een focus op Supply Chain Management;
  • Heb je kennis van of interesse in processen zoals inkoop, voorraadbeheer, warehousemanagement, logistiek en orderverwerking;
  • Kijk je verder dan alleen de applicatie en verdiep je je graag in de bedrijfsprocessen van de klant;
  • Communiceer je gemakkelijk met verschillende stakeholders;
  • Neem je eigenaarschap over cases en klantvragen;
  • Houd je overzicht wanneer je voor meerdere klanten werkt en verschillende prioriteiten hebt;
  • Denk je proactief mee over procesverbeteringen en mogelijke optimalisaties;
  • Vind je het leuk om langdurige klantrelaties op te bouwen.

Wat verzorgen wij?

  • Bij HSO reis je niet alleen voor een baan maar voor een carrière vol ontdekkingen. Naast een marktconform salaris en een prestatiegerichte bonus, krijg je praktische benodigdheden en beleving:

  • Mobiliteitsvergoeding waarbij je of een auto kunt leasen of het bedrag toe kunt
    voegen aan je salaris. Daar bovenop krijg 100% betaald van de ov-kosten;
  • Je kunt deelnemen aan het leasefietsplan;
  • EUR 65,- netto vitaliteitsbudget, we vinden het belangrijk dat we gezond blijven en een veilige werkplek hebben, zowel op kantoor als remote;
  • Op dag één start jouw onboardingprogramma, daarnaast krijg je een persoonlijk studiebudget dat je kunt inzetten voor jouw professionele ontwikkeling en ontvang je ook een GoodHabitz account, een online trainingstool voor je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.
  • 25 vakantiedagen + optie om 10 extra te kopen; workations mogelijk voor wie écht nieuwe houvast zoekt;
  • Dagelijkse verzorgde lunch, bedrijfsfeesten, sportactiviteiten en wekelijkse borrels om onze gezamenlijke reis te versterken.

Onze wereldwijde route

Als Microsoft Inner Circle-partner en internationaal opererend bedrijf biedt HSO jou toegang tot best practices, certificeringen en een wereldwijd netwerk van experts. Samen met ruim 2200 getalenteerde medewerkers in Europa, Azië en Noord-Amerika verlenen we ondersteuning op lokaal en internationaal niveau aan industriële bedrijven, retailers, financiële en zakelijke dienstverleners en overheidsinstellingen. iTradeNetwork's Leadership Principles

iTradeNetwork’s purpose is to feed the world — and everything we do is guided by the principles below. Every team member is expected to embody and champion these principles across the organization.

Bias for Action

We value speed and avoid analysis paralysis. We develop conviction, make informed decisions quickly, and take calculated risks to maintain momentum — knowing that swift progress is essential for innovation and growth.

Customer Obsession

We work relentlessly to delight our customers. We work backward from their needs to solve pain points and create solutions that surprise and earn their loyalty. We obsess over customers, not competitors.

Data & Metrics Driven

We operate with facts, not opinions. We dive deep into data and use metrics to measure progress, ground every decision in rigorous analysis, and push for clarity and measurable outcomes.

Raise the Bar

We continuously push for improvement — in ourselves, our teams, and the company. We hire and develop exceptional talent, setting ever-higher standards that elevate performance and drive excellence.

Operational Excellence Through Process

We build lasting processes that optimize for efficiency. By developing, testing, and documenting each process, we create consistency and scale through automation, enabling continuous improvement across the business.

Ownership Mindset

We take responsibility for our work and aim for long-term success. We use resources wisely, stay accountable, and roll up our sleeves to get things done — no task is beneath us.

Earn Trust

We build trust through integrity, transparency, and mutual respect. We communicate openly, own our mistakes, listen actively, and remain open to feedback as an opportunity for growth.

JOB SUMMARY

The Director, Product Management acts as the CEO of a set of products, assuming responsibility for the product strategy, financial outcomes, customer experience, and user experience design for the product solutions at iTradeNetwork. Reporting to the Chief Product Officer, the role requires a unique blend of business acumen, design skills, technology expertise, and a strong drive to exceed growth expectations. title: Staff Software Engineer, AI Platform & Infrastructure
description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

The Software Engineer Opportunity

The team that built Jeeva AI is building Digital Workers, a new suite of autonomous agents for identity operations and security inside Okta. The team works directly with Todd McKinnon, Okta's co-founder and CEO, with the opportunity to bring this product to Okta's 20,000+ customers. You will help shape the product with the ownership and pace of a startup and the resources of a public company.

You will build the backend and AWS platform that keep these workers running around the clock. The team owns services, connectors, workflow execution, data and production reliability. You will write Python services and infrastructure code that let workers make approved changes and preserve evidence.

About You

Reliable builder: You design for failure and prove that recovery works.

Hands-on engineer: You write production services and improve the tools engineers use every day.

Strong owner: You follow changes through deployment, monitoring and production support.

What you will be doing

  • Build Python FastAPI services, data models and reusable connectors for Okta, AWS, ServiceNow and enterprise applications.
  • Implement durable execution with Step Functions, SQS and EventBridge. Handle approval waits, rate limits, duplicate events and safe retries.
  • Manage PostgreSQL schemas, indexes, query performance and pgvector retrieval. Enforce tenant isolation across APIs, storage and credentials.
  • Build model API access for OpenAI, Anthropic and supported AWS paths, including credentials, quotas, timeouts and cost controls.
  • Add an analytics pipeline for worker events, traces, tokens, findings and verified outcomes. Evaluate ClickHouse and comparable systems such as BigQuery.
  • Create reliable usage records and reconciliation. Prevent retries, duplicate findings and incomplete work from being counted as new outcomes.
  • Build deployment pipelines, infrastructure as code, observability and safe release controls across development, staging and production.
  • Implement scoped write services, kill switches, audit retention and backup recovery. Test failures and verify that sensitive changes actually took effect.

What you will bring to the role

  • Experience building and operating production backend or distributed systems, with strong coding skills in Python or a comparable language.
  • Hands-on AWS experience with APIs, queues, containers, networking, IAM and databases.
  • Strong SQL and data modeling skills. Experience diagnosing database performance and asynchronous system failures.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code, deployment automation, observability and production incident response.
  • Sound judgment about customer data, tenant isolation, credentials and safe changes to external systems.

Scope by level

Senior: Own a backend or platform component, including deployment, tests and production operation.

Staff: Lead a domain such as execution, tenant security, data infrastructure or reliability across teams.

Principal: Set shared backend and platform contracts, resolve system tradeoffs and implement foundational services.

Our stack

Python FastAPI, AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, API Gateway and containers. Data and security use RDS PostgreSQL, pgvector, S3 Object Lock, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch and CloudTrail. The frontend uses React and AWS Amplify.

OpenAI and Anthropic model integrations are planned. We are also adding an agent harness and dedicated analytics. ClickHouse is a hiring focus for analytics, and BigQuery or equivalent experience is relevant. The harness and analytics choices remain open.

And extra credit for

  • ClickHouse, BigQuery or comparable analytics systems, event ingestion and usage metering.
  • Multi-tenant SaaS, OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SCIM or enterprise connector development.
  • Deploying agent frameworks, including Claude Agent SDK, Codex SDK, Strands Agents, Deep Agents or LangGraph. Prior identity experience is optional.

  • Take ownership of customer issues and escalate them through the appropriate channels when additional support is needed.
